did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm’s title identifies it as a maskil and attributes it to Ethan the Ezrahite, presenting it as a psalm of reflection and instruction.
Did you know? The psalmist commits to singing of the Lord’s lovingkindness forever and making his faithfulness known to every generation, turning praise into an intergenerational message.
Did you know? At the heart of the psalm is the covenant made with David: the Lord declares that he has made a covenant with his chosen one and sworn to David, his servant.
Did you know? The psalm portrays the heavens and the assembly of the holy ones as acknowledging the Lord’s wonders and faithfulness, emphasizing that no one in the heavenly realm compares with him.
Did you know? The Lord’s control over the sea is presented as a sign of his power: he rules over the surging sea and stills its waves when they rise.
Did you know? According to the psalm, righteousness and justice are the foundation of God’s throne, while lovingkindness and truth go before him.
Did you know? The people’s happiness is linked here to knowing the joyful shout—or proclamation—and to walking in the light of the Lord’s presence.
Did you know? David is portrayed as the one whom the Lord found, anointed with holy oil, strengthened with his hand, and promised to protect from his enemies.

Did you know? The covenant with David’s line also includes moral responsibility: if his descendants abandon the law and commandments, they will be punished. Nevertheless, the Lord declares that he will not withdraw his lovingkindness or break his covenant.

Did you know? In the later part of the psalm, a sharp tension emerges between the promise of David’s throne forever and the reality of the kingdom’s downfall, the disgrace of the crown, the breaching of the fortifications, and defeat in battle.
